facts.statement: The IFSCA Compliance Handbook for AML/CTF/KYC is based on the IFSCA (AML, CTF and KYC) Guidelines 2022 together with PMLA 2002, UAPA 1967 and the WMD Act 2005.

The AML compliance roadmap has 9 steps: Principal Officer appointment, FINGate registration, EWRA, policies, CDD, TFS, STR reporting, governance, and record-keeping; the AML PO must be management-level with adequate seniority.
The Enterprise-Wide Risk Assessment (EWRA) must be reviewed at least every 2 years or upon significant change.
Periodic Customer Due Diligence review frequency: high-risk customers annually, medium-risk every 3 years, low-risk every 5 years.

Targeted Financial Sanctions require freezing and reporting to the Nodal Officer within 24 hours; STRs are filed to FIU-IND through mandatory FINGate 2.0 registration; CKYCR upload is required for account-based relationships with Indian nationals.
AML/CFT records must be retained for a minimum of 6 years from the end of the business relationship or completion of the transaction.

The IFSCA KYC Registration Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2025 were notified in April 2025 (notified 11 April; approved at the 27 March 2025 Authority meeting) to standardise KYC processes, enhance data security and strengthen AML/CFT across IFSC entities, with net worth and fit-and-proper requirements.
facts.detail: The first KRA was operationalised around the Global Securities Markets Conclave 2.0 in February 2026.

facts.statement: From 31 October 2025, Video-based Customer Identification (V-CIP) is enabled for low-risk NRIs from specified jurisdictions to ease onboarding.
